about: Frames are drawn from these numbers (HTML/CSS/SVG), never from a bitmap. Fractions refer to the body width (bezel, rim, radii of the body) or to the SHORT side of the screen (screen_radius, cutout, bars). The screen rectangle takes the capture's aspect; the body follows with a constant bezel. A yearly device change is an edit of this file.

iphone.generation: current iPhone class with a Dynamic Island pill (generic drawing, no vendor artwork)

ipad.generation: current iPad class, uniform bezel, no cut-out (generic drawing)

android-phone.generation: current Pixel-class Android phone with a centred punch-hole (generic drawing)

android-tablet.generation: current Android tablet class, uniform bezel (generic drawing)

neutral-phone.generation: platform-neutral phone, no cut-out, no glyphs: safe for both stores

browser.generation: neutral browser window: three dots and an address pill, no vendor chrome

macos-window.generation: desktop app window: three coloured dots and a centred title

none.generation: frameless: the capture as a rounded card with a shadow

landscape.why: By default UIKit hides the status bar of a view controller in a vertically compact environment, which is every iPhone in landscape

landscape.why: 24 dp on a 412 dp short side: status_bar_height_landscape is status_bar_height_portrait (24dp), and SystemBarUtils takes max(top cutout inset, 24dp + waterfall); a punch-hole on the short side adds no top inset in landscape. Glyphs keep their portrait size, centred on the thinner bar
